sections.text: One trial tests CD38 as a target in myasthenia gravis, a Phase 2 study sponsored by Takeda that completed in 2022.
The drug in the trial is tak-079, a CD38-targeting antibody intended to deplete plasma cells.
CD38-targeting antibodies are approved for multiple myeloma, with daratumumab indicated in several combination regimens for that disease.
Serious adverse reactions with CD38 antibodies include infections, neutropenia, thrombocytopenia, and hypersensitivity reactions.

A 2026 preclinical study demonstrated that an anti-CD38 antibody fused to acetylcholine receptor antigen (ACE) selectively depleted autoreactive plasma cells, reduced autoantibody titers, and improved disease scores in a myasthenia gravis model.
Anti-CD19 CAR T-cell therapy has shown durable remission in refractory myasthenia gravis patients, representing a competing cellular approach to B-cell depletion.

read: Mechanism evidence: CD38 targeting via antibodies depletes plasma cells and has shown preclinical efficacy in MG models.
Competitive position: Limited clinical activity in MG despite approval in myeloma; faces competition from anti-CD19 CAR T and other B-cell targeting agents.
Open questions: Will CD38 inhibition achieve durable remission in MG? How does it compare to broader B-cell depletion strategies?
would_change: New Phase 2 results from Takeda would clarify efficacy.
Head-to-head comparison with anti-CD19 therapies would affect competitive assessment.
Emergence of additional CD38 trials in MG would signal increased confidence.
